title: UPDATE: Nscale Investors Demand $16B IPO Valuation After Site Failures
summary:
Shareholders in the British AI data center provider are pushing the company to reduce its expected worth during a planned stock market listing after several operational setbacks. Investors are urging Nscale to target a valuation in the range of $16 billion to $19 billion, a drop from the previous $30 billion target, as the firm seeks to raise as much as $3 billion. The company has aimed to list as soon as this month, but now faces opposition to its pricing targets following a series of losses in its site pipeline.

The pressure comes after Microsoft canceled a deal to rent 23,000 GPUs at a site in Essex because power may not be available until the 2030s. Microsoft and Anthropic account for about 85% of Nscale's $103 billion contract pipeline, making the loss of an anchor tenant particularly damaging. Other assets are similarly troubled; Nscale's site in Norway operates only 6.4 MW of a planned 30 MW following a December fire and cooling leaks. Nvidia previously invested $1 billion in Nscale's pre-IPO convertible notes to support its buildout.

selectedTweets.text:
🦔Nscale, the British AI data center company planning an IPO at up to $35 billion, is six months behind on its flagship site in Norway, Bloomberg reports. Only 6.4 of a planned 30 megawatts run there after cooling leaks, a December fire and construction delays, and late capacity has already cost it millions in penalties. Back in March, investors valued the whole company at $14.6 billion.

My Take
The pitch is $103 billion in signed contracts. About 85% of that comes from two customers, Microsoft and Anthropic, and Nscale admits it hasn’t lined up the money or the chips for Anthropic’s $44.6 billion deal yet. Anthropic can cancel parts of that contract with no penalty if capacity shows up late, and Nscale can’t get 30 megawatts running on time in Norway. A contract the customer can walk away from doesn’t count for much as backlog.

Nvidia also put $1 billion into Nscale’s pre-IPO convertible notes, so the chipmaker is once again funding a company that buys its chips, same as it did with CoreWeave. The grid power for Nscale’s next big Norway expansion probably won’t arrive before 2037 either. My guess is the price comes down well below $35 billion before this lists, or the date slides into next year.

Hedgie🤗

selectedTweets.text:
Everything that happened in the data center world today (Oct 18, 2026)

The chips are still sold out. The money and the megawatts aren't.

NEOCLOUDS + FINANCING
- Microsoft pulled out as anchor tenant of Nscale's Loughton, Essex AI site after grid officials said power isn't expected until the 2030s. Nscale says it's still committed and is looking at other power (Telegraph, Reuters)
- Nscale's Glomfjord site in Norway is about six months late, with 6.4MW of 30MW live (Bloomberg)
- Some of the $38B loan behind Oracle's Texas and Wisconsin builds has traded around 90 cents, some debt tied to its New Mexico site near 80. Insuring $1M of SoftBank debt costs over $40,000 vs under $27,000 at the start of the year. Barclays says risky AI debt spreads are up 50%+ in six months (NYT)
- Junk buyers are increasingly freezing out tech startups after CoreWeave's bonds hit 15% (Bloomberg)

NEW PROJECTS + PUSHBACK
- RegLayer counts 47+ large US data center projects delayed, withdrawn or suspended this year. Bernstein thinks only about 35% of planned US builds get finished (FT)
- Digital Realty plans a ~1GW campus in Kokomo, Indiana: 476 acres, full build possible by 2033, no tax breaks per the city (DCD)
- An Italian mayor halted a 576MW application billed as the country's largest. Its region has 13.13GW of grid requests (DCD)

POWER + GRID
- Pennsylvania's governor petitioned to join PPL's rate case, a first in at least 15 years. He wants big data centers in their own customer class, paying their own costs. PPL's advanced pipeline is 31.8GW (PA governor's office, The Inference)

CHIPS + POLICY
- Taiwan plans US parks for the small suppliers behind TSMC, Nvidia and Foxconn. The first, in Texas, could cost up to $4B (Bloomberg via CNA)
- China's Pengcheng Cloud Brain III began trial runs on 10,000P of Huawei Ascend compute, heading to 16,000P (Tonghuashun)

MEMORY
- Samsung will use TSMC 3nm for the base die of Nvidia's custom HBM, per industry sources. Nvidia asked Samsung, SK hynix and Micron all to do it. The paper says that gets up to 30% more bandwidth and 15% less power than standard HBM4E (Seoul Economic Daily)
- Same report cites UBS: 2027 HBM demand up 91% vs supply about 10% short (Seoul Economic Daily)
- CXMT guided nine-month profit of RMB131-132.5B. Backing out the first half, Q3 sales rose 15-20% vs Q2 but profit only about 1-4% (CXMT filing, Yicai)
- Follow-up: Samsung fell 17.8% and SK hynix 24.3% Oct 12-16, worst weeks since 2008. Foreigners net sold ₩11.2T of Kospi stocks, 79% in those two (Korea Herald)

PARTS + PACKAGING
- Kingboard raised thin glass-cloth CCL and prepreg 15%, its eighth hike this year. Panasonic told customers some general CCL goes up 200% from January (Commercial Times)
- A Goldman basket of Asian AI hardware fell 11% last week. Samsung Electro-Mechanics -23%, Unimicron -14% (Bloomberg)

NETWORKING + OPTICS
- Salience Labs raised $125M for optical circuit switches, with AMD and Intel investing. It's at 64 ports and wants 256 (DCD)

MARKETS
- The SOX fell 3.8% Friday, its eighth straight loss and longest streak since 2008, down 16% since Oct 6 (Investing)

What it all means: Microsoft walking from Loughton looks like a power call, not a demand call. But that's how the squeeze hits neoclouds. The tenant can walk, the developer is stuck with the land and the debt. A lease on a site without firm power is a free option for the hyperscaler. Nvidia is also pushing all three memory makers onto a TSMC base die. Great for Nvidia's leverage, and if it sticks, TSMC gets paid whichever memory maker wins. The number I'd watch is CXMT: 15-20% more sales for flat profit is a seller's own data saying DRAM price gains are slowing. SK hynix on Oct 28 says if that's China-only. The capex number doesn't get cut. The delivered megawatts do.
